comment: Ownership manifest for everything this repository persists between or across CI runs. Cache admission is decided by the stability of an artifact's identity key relative to its size, NOT by whether GitHub happens to call the store a 'cache' or an 'artifact'. Every persisting step in .github/workflows/ must be classified here. Adding a store means amending this file in the same PR, so the edge shows up in review rather than as one line in a workflow nobody diffs.

tiers.cook: Tier 1. External dependency compilation plus build-script / native (cc-rs, bindgen) outputs. The identity key is the locked dependency graph, which moves rarely relative to its size, so the entry is durable and worth persisting across runs. Swatinem/rust-cache also lands here -- it prunes workspace-member artifacts, examples and target/*/incremental before saving, so what survives is the dependency graph -- which is exactly the problem soldr#2996 resolves: two implementations of one tier, with the third-party one carrying the load. soldr#3047 removed it from `_ci-cross-build-linux.yml` (the lane soldr#2996 measured cook on), `_build-and-test.yml`, and both pep517 lanes; the last producer -- `ci.yml`'s bootstrap driver, which builds soldr with bare cargo before any soldr exists -- was retired when CACHE-025 dropped its exceptions (zackees/ci.yml, maintainer decision 2026-10-02); that build is now uncached on a binary-cache miss, and no Swatinem/rust-cache producer remains. zackees/ci.yml#209 retired the `ci.yml` wheel-cross producer outright (the lane has a soldr, so no exception applies; it is now uncached). soldr#3121 retired the third producer, `bootstrap-e2e`, entirely (no replacement rust-cache) to fund cook on the new MSVC/aarch64-gnu cross lanes. `soldr dylint cook` prepares the Dylint analysis and UI-test dependency trees under this tier; it is content-addressed on the lint crate's locked graph and the exact nightly, and it fills an in-run target tree rather than uploading one.
tiers.zccache-unit: Tier 2. Per-compilation-unit, content-addressed compiler outputs held by the embedded zccache service. Safe by construction: the key IS the hash of the compiler inputs, so a stale entry cannot be served. Durable, and deliberately still live in normal lanes -- soldr#2931 bans persisting LINKED products and bulk target/ snapshots, not content-addressed per-unit caching.
tiers.none: Tier 3. Everything else. Not admitted to any cross-run reusable compiler/dependency store. Run-scoped uploads (logs, diagnostics, benchmark rows, wheels kept for inspection) live here: they are retained for humans and are never restored into a later build. Linked TEST products are permanently Tier 3 -- test binaries, benches, examples built for tests, doctest products, test debug sidecars and test-specific incremental state may not enter cook, an rlib cache, a broad target/ cache, a compiler-cache archive, or any other cross-run reusable store. linked TEST PRODUCTS -- test binaries, harness executables, and fixture crates built for UI tests -- are Tier 3 wherever they live, INCLUDING `target/dylint/tests`; but the third-party dependency rlibs and build-script outputs that same directory holds are Tier 1 by identity-key stability (their key is the lint crate's `Cargo.lock`), and they are prepared by `soldr dylint cook --tree tests` (soldr#3042). soldr#3003's lesson was that scoping to a DIRECTORY instead of an artifact tier was the defect; a content-addressed cook of the dependency layer is the only admitted path for that layer, and `target/dylint/tests` itself remains excluded from every `actions/cache` key.

exceptions.attestation-evidence: A tiny per-gate ci-attestation side entry (zackees/ci.yml#198, GATE-010; soldr#3534): the compact JSON of one stamp-valid `Ci-Attestation:` trailer, keyed by its gate and its commit's human-readable, ancestor-defining lineage label (att1-<gate>-m<b>-c<k>-<sha10>[-pr-<N>]). It is evidence, not a build product: nothing restores it into a compile; later runs LIST the keys (GET-only REST) to decide which caches are valid to hydrate. A few hundred bytes each.
exceptions.release-deliverable: The shipped output. Its lifetime is the release, not a build; it is uploaded to be published, never restored into a compile.
exceptions.pinned-immutable-download: A third-party download pinned to an exact, immutable version (rustup toolchain, xwin MSVC CRT+SDK slice, Apple SDK 14.5, crates.io registry sources). The identity key is the version string and the bytes never change under it, so the entry is as stable as a key can be.
exceptions.dylint-foundation: The ci-test Dylint foundation: cargo-dylint / dylint-link plus the one exact nightly every lint manifest declares. Keyed on that nightly, and required by contract to never reuse or invalidate the stable target tree (CLAUDE.md, ci-test verb).
exceptions.cache-experiment: The cache is the subject under test. These workflows measure cold/warm behaviour, cook sizing, target-cache slices or parent-cache sharing, so the guard cannot constrain what they persist without destroying the measurement. Listed explicitly in experiment_workflows.
exceptions.same-run-transport: A bundle handed from one job to another INSIDE one workflow run via upload-artifact/download-artifact. Not a cache: it is keyed by run id, never restored into a later run, and discarded on retention expiry. This is the only sanctioned way a linked test archive may be moved to a target-run lane -- it must be compact and budgeted, and it must never be written to a cross-run store.
exceptions.bootstrap-driver-binary: The host bootstrap `soldr` that DRIVES a lane (spawns the broker, prepares blessed SDKs). Keyed on the exact commit SHA, so the key is maximally stable; one binary, no test products. It is the compiler for the lane, not an output under test. Beyond the four exceptions named in soldr#2931; recorded here because the class exists in-tree and needed a name.

family_groups_comment: soldr#3618: ci.toml [cache.family] is the ONE declaration of every cache family's key prefix and size; this object holds no byte numbers. Each group lists the ci.toml families it owns (ci_toml_families; every ci.toml family belongs to exactly one group), the ownership entries R7 checks, and the janitor's `evict` policy (lru | newest | newest-per-lineage | absent = never evicted for budget), which ci.toml's own `evict` ("lru" only) cannot spell. .github/scripts/cache_families.py composes the janitor's budget: a group's allocation is the SUM of its members' ci.toml footprints (CACHE-004 arithmetic), total_max_bytes is the sum over all families, and fail_total_bytes is ci.toml [cache].budget. History: soldr#3047 introduced the per-family allocation here; the 2026-09-01 measurement it was sized from is tests/fixtures/actions-cache/listing-2026-09-01.json.

attestation-evidence.evict_rationale: Evidence for hydration decisions; losing an old entry only makes a later run pick an older (or no) attested ancestor. The PR janitor deletes a closed PR's entries by their -pr-<N> suffix.
attestation-evidence.rationale: zackees/ci.yml#198 pilot: one ~330-byte entry per attested gate per PR head (7 gates). Carved from experiment-lanes, which evicts least-recently-used.

pinned-immutable-download.evict_rationale: Pinned, sha-verified downloads any job can re-fetch. The newest entry of each lineage (the key with digit runs normalized, e.g. soldr-mini-v2-linux-x64-glibc-v<ver>) is what current jobs restore and is never evicted; older versions of the same download are evicted least-recently-used first until the family fits (zackees/ci.yml#6).
pinned-immutable-download.rationale: Version-keyed immutable downloads. Bytes never change under the key, so these are the cheapest entries in the store; they are budgeted rather than exempt because per-target keys multiply.

bootstrap-driver-binary.rationale: One ~20-24 MB driver per commit SHA. Keyed on github.sha, so it cannot be restored across commits and cannot be main-gated; it churns instead of accumulating.

cook-layer.rationale: setup-soldr's cook archives for the cross lanes; Tier 1 and the layer that replaced cross-build rust-cache. The key embeds the rustc commit, lockfile hash and soldr version and setup-soldr/cook exposes no save-if input, so this family cannot be main-gated from inside this repo (soldr#3047 step 7). If it exceeds this allocation, the key shape is a zackees/setup-soldr change and the finding belongs in soldr#3039. soldr#3121 added aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu (~450 MiB base archive each), funded by retiring the bootstrap-e2e rust-cache and trimming headroom elsewhere.

dylint-foundation.rationale: The ci-test Dylint foundation (soldr#3017) plus setup-soldr's ci-tests layer. dylint-foundation-* is main-gated via a restore/save split in soldr#3047 and pruned to its newest generation on main (soldr#3216: the key hashes the lint sources, so each lint change otherwise leaves a ~413 MiB generation behind). dylint-driver-* (soldr#2349) is the cargo-dylint driver plus the prepared-plan marker, version-keyed and under 1 MiB. The dylint-nightly-* toolchain cache soldr#2349 also added here was retired by soldr#3216: at 452 MiB it put this family at ~0.85 GiB against its allocation, no other family had measured headroom to cover it, and it saved about 15 s per host run.

setup-soldr-action-stores.evict_rationale: Superseded lock/toolchain generations are the safe-prune class (soldr#3545's toolchain-aware lineage in check_cache_budget.py) and are deleted before any budget eviction runs; this policy makes the allocation reachable for whatever safe-prune cannot explain. The keys end in 16-hex hashes whose letters defeat newest-per-lineage digit normalization -- the same reason zccache-unit declares newest (soldr#3458) -- so only the newest main store generation is protected from budget eviction and the rest go least-recently-used first until the family fits.
setup-soldr-action-stores.rationale: Content-addressed per-unit zccache stores plus setup-soldr's own registry slice, written by the action-smoke and benchmark lanes. The dogfood store is main-gated by a restore/save split in soldr#3047. Recognized buildcache-v2 and cargoregistry-v1 entries retain their platform's newest current-main-lock toolchain store; an entry on that platform with an older lock OR an older toolchain hash is a superseded generation and is reclaimed (soldr#3545 -- a toolchain bump changes the toolchain hash while Cargo.lock often does not, which left a 1.43 GiB family over its 1.30 GiB allocation with no rule that could ever select the stale half). A platform with no current-lock store, unknown formats, and namespaced keys remain protected.

experiment-lanes.evict_rationale: No required job restores these keys: every producer is an opt-in experiment or perf workflow (experiment_workflows). The janitor evicts least-recently-used entries down to the group's footprint, costing an experiment at most one warm start; without it the six-hourly budget run stayed permanently red (zackees/ci.yml#6).
experiment-lanes.rationale: Workflows where the cache IS the subject under test. Deliberately NOT main-gated: perf-matrix.yml runs only on main and perf/** branches, so a main-only save rule would leave the lane PERF.md calls the most important in the repo permanently cold. Budgeted instead, so the measurement lanes are bounded without being broken. perf-matrix retains only its exact-source soldr-bin cache (same-source reruns avoid compilation); the former perf-registry-soldr rust-cache prefix is registered only for safe retirement and has no producer.

zccache-unit.evict_rationale: Only the newest main generation is restored by a required job (restore-keys pick the newest match), so older generations are evicted least-recently-used first until the family fits. The keys end in a lockfile hash whose letters defeat newest-per-lineage digit normalization (soldr#3458).
zccache-unit.rationale: store_cap_bytes is the UNCOMPRESSED on-disk trim cap; the group's ci.toml footprint is the compressed Actions budget. Trimming the on-disk store to max_bytes evicted the ci-test driver build's ~381 dependency units every run, leaving that step at 0 hits (soldr#3458: measured working set with the driver units 2.92 GiB; a saved generation compresses about 4x). The ci-test host lane's cross-run compiler store: soldr#3041's Tier-2 per-unit object store (zccache-unit-*), restored by lockfile-hash prefix, saved on main only, and pruned and trimmed to this allocation before the save (soldr#3120, soldr#3252). Allocation rebalanced by 0.05 GiB to rust-cache-residual in 2026-09 (live usage was 0.82 GiB) and by a further 0.40 GiB on 2026-10-01 (live 0.00 GiB; 1.55 GiB still covers the ~0.73 GiB compressed working set soldr#3458 measured). zackees/ci.yml#209 returned 0.90 GiB from rust-cache-residual when it retired the wheel-cross rust-cache producer (live 2026-10-02: two main generations, 1.54 GiB). soldr#3043's stable cook archives (stable-cook-*) shared this family until soldr#3396 retired them: that prototype restored the previous lockfile's cook directory through a restore-keys prefix and never pruned it, so one entry grew to 2.8 GB. stable-cook-* is now a retired prefix in check_cache_budget.py, and check_cache_ownership.py R8 rejects any new appending prefix-fallback cache without a registered prune step. The ci.toml prefix is a contract: a producer keyed outside every declared family is rejected by the gate as an unregistered producer.

setup_soldr_layers.comment: setup-soldr provisions several independent reuse layers. Each is gated on its own input, NOT on the `cache` umbrella (soldr#2451) -- which is why this repo's self-build lanes spell out `false` for all of them: this repo IS soldr and no self-build lane may restore a prebuilt soldr binary. Only layers a workflow turns ON get an entry below. soldr#2996 removed the target-cache layers entirely: the thin slice was a freshness slice whose library bytes zccache had to reproduce anyway, and `full` was a banned bulk target/ snapshot. soldr cook is the only durable compiler cache.

cache.rationale: The action's own zccache compiler store under `cache-dir`. Content-addressed per unit.

build-cache.rationale: zccache compiler store keyed on toolchain + commit. Content-addressed per unit; disabled in every self-build lane here.

cargo-registry-cache.rationale: crates.io source tarballs, immutable under their version. Disabled in every self-build lane here.

cook.rationale: The `setup-soldr/cook` subaction: prebuilt external-dependency and build-script outputs under target/<triple>/<profile>/build/*/out/.

soldr-mini-cache.rationale: A prebuilt, released soldr binary keyed on its version. Disabled in every self-build lane here (soldr#2451).

solo-toolchain-cache.rationale: A pinned Rust toolchain under the action's managed RUSTUP_HOME. Disabled in every self-build lane here.

ci-tests.rationale: Provisions cargo-dylint / dylint-link plus the exact declared nightly for the ci-test Dylint plan.

entries.rationale: Per-gate ci-attestation evidence (compact JSON) keyed by lineage label; listed, never restored into a build.
The 1.95.0 toolchain tree, keyed on the exact version; immutable bytes under an immutable key.
The smoke-tested binary retained for inspection; nothing downloads it into a later build.
Run-scoped diagnostics for humans; never restored.
Run-scoped diagnostics for humans; never restored.
Same immutable, version-keyed toolchain tree as the bootstrap template.
Provisions the ci-test Dylint foundation once, on its own nightly, separate from the stable target tree.

entries.step: Restore Dylint libraries and analysis trees
entries.rationale: The Dylint libraries and analysis target trees, keyed (v2, soldr#2349) on the exact nightly every lint manifest declares, the lint sources, their Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock dependency graphs, and their .cargo/config.toml (which carries the `-C linker=dylint-link` rustflag -- a v1 blind spot that let a linker-config change restore a stale tree instead of invalidating it). 638s/run of byte-identical cold work that no other layer can serve: Swatinem/rust-cache deletes target/dylint/** at save, and dylint_cook_acceptance.py shows a per-unit object cache alone still misses. target/dylint/tests is DELIBERATELY excluded -- soldr#3012 measured it at 1.9 GiB of UI-test products, which is tier 3 and may not enter any cross-run store (soldr#3017). As of soldr#3042 the third-party dependency layer inside that directory is prepared in-run by the `build-and-test-dylint-tests-cook` entry below, so 'the UI-test stages stay cold by design' now applies only to the linked UI-test products themselves; the directory exclusion is unchanged.

entries.step: Restore Dylint driver and prepared-plan marker
entries.rationale: soldr#2349: the cargo-dylint driver binary (`<SOLDR_CACHE_DIR>/dylint/drivers/<nightly>-<host>/`) and the warm-run prepared-plan TTL marker (`<SOLDR_CACHE_DIR>/dylint/prepared/v1/`), keyed on the resolved nightly identity plus the pinned cargo-dylint version. SOLDR_CACHE_DIR is exported to a `runner.temp`-rooted, per-run-wiped directory (soldr#1241's cache-domain step), so both otherwise go cold and the driver is re-fetched from the soldr-toolchain catalogue every run even though its identity never changed between runs. Same nightly-keyed identity class as build-and-test-dylint-foundation, not a new tier.
Run-scoped build XML + compile journals for toolchain-home and recompile-storm triage.

entries.step: Reuse shared source driver if already available
entries.rationale: Opportunistically receives the exact-workflow-SHA dev-profile Soldr driver already produced for cross lanes. Missing or mismatched provenance falls back to the identical local dev-profile source build; it is never restored across workflow runs.

Saved on main only since soldr#3102 (restore/save split; PRs restore main's generation through the prefix restore-key). Content-addressed per-unit compiler outputs for the ci-test host lane; the path selects cache/zccache/daemon-state only, so the compile journals (cache/zccache/history) and session logs (cache/zccache/logs) that the build-logs artifact ships stay run-scoped and outside the entry. Not a new cache family: zccache-unit is already declared durable and live in normal lanes. soldr#3039 Phase 0.
entries.notes: The service's own versioned log directory (daemon-state/embedded-v1/v<VERSION>/logs/) is INSIDE the selected path and is stored with the objects; zccache owns its rotation, and an actions/cache path negation could not exclude it. The lane scrubs staging/ and every lock/socket/pid file from the tree after the daemon stops and before the post-step tar, mirroring archive_always_excludes_cache_path in crates/soldr-cache/src/cache_lib/save_inventory.rs -- those files are never cache payload, they race the tar, and restoring them breaks a later daemon start. No per-entry size cap is set: the embedded budget (ZCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE_BYTES / ZCCACHE_CACHE_SIZE_PERCENT) is the one real cap. The per-family allocation belongs to soldr#3047, which sizes this store's share at 2.0 GiB; this entry states that share and does not enforce it.

entries.rationale: The xwin CRT+SDK slice, keyed on MANAGED_XWIN_CACHE_VERSION; the bytes never change under that key.
Apple SDK 14.5 darwin-x86_64 slice, keyed on the catalogue version and shape.
Apple SDK 14.5 darwin-aarch64 slice, keyed on the catalogue version and shape.
Receives the one bootstrap driver built earlier in the same run, instead of every cross lane rebuilding it.
Fallback path for manual callers with no bootstrap artifact; keyed on the exact commit SHA, one binary, no test products.
Prebuilt external-dependency and cc-rs build-script outputs for the (profile, triple) shape under test.
Carries dist/package/ plus the linked nextest archive to the same run's target-run lane. Legal ONLY as transport: it is run-keyed and must never be written to a cross-run store.
entries.notes: Compactness/size budget for this bundle is owned by the lane itself (soldr#2931 phases 3-4), not by check_cache_ownership.py.

entries.rationale: Run-scoped logs and archived compile journals; never restored.
The receiving half of cross-build-test-transport: cross-built products executed on a native runner in the same run.
Run-scoped daemon smoke logs.
Run-scoped toolchain-ensure/doctor JSON for triage.
Run-scoped daemon smoke logs.
Version-keyed, immutable toolchain tree shared with the other soldr workflows.
The dev-profile bootstrap driver keyed on the exact commit SHA (deliberately not hashFiles, which misses submodule content).
Fans the single bootstrap driver out to every cross lane in the same run.
Receiving half of ci-bootstrap-artifact-upload for the `soldr wheel` lane.
A CI wheel kept for inspection; the shipped wheel is built by auto-release.yml.
Version-keyed, immutable toolchain tree.
Content-addressed per-unit compiler store; the trend job builds the commit under test through the released wrapper.

entries.step: Upload canary output as workflow artifact
entries.rationale: Measurement rows published to Pages; never restored into a build.
One bootstrap driver built once and consumed by every cross job in the same run.
Receiving half of cross-all-bootstrap-upload.
The per-target shipped `.tar.zst`; its lifetime is the release, not a build.

entries.step: Upload per-target stats / Download all stats / Upload summary
entries.rationale: Timing rows and the rolled-up summary; reporting only.

entries.step: Upload result row / Download result rows
entries.rationale: One JSON row per matrix cell, merged into a report; nothing is compiled from them.
`release-soldr-<target>` archives and `pypi-soldr-<target>` wheels staged for publication.
Smoke, checksum and publish jobs re-download the staged deliverables inside the same run.
The action's own runtime state under a `cache-dir` deliberately disjoint from the soldr build under test.
The zccache store for the dogfood build. Content-addressed per unit -- exactly the store soldr#2931 keeps live; the ban is on linked products and bulk target/ snapshots.
Run-scoped JSON snapshots and command logs retained for soldr#2878 analysis; no later build restores them.
Measures the zero-dependency baseline build; what it caches is part of the measurement.
Compares today's single-layer cache against a layered alternative; the cache IS the subject under test.
Acceptance for the Dylint foundation cache.
Acceptance for cook behaviour under the Dylint plan.
Cold/warm demo: it deliberately seeds and purges its own cache namespace.
The perf sweep; cache state is an independent variable of the measurement.
Per-triple release binary plus the x86_64 nextest archive, handed to the combine job of the SAME dispatch-only run (3-day retention); never restored into a later build.
The lipo'd universal2 binary and test payload for the macOS guest job of the same run; inspection only, nothing downloads it into a compile.
Guest logs and test results retained for humans.
Receives the verified test archive and native Nextest executable from the cross-build job of this one dispatch run; never restored by a later build.

entries.step: Upload probe measurements and guest log
entries.rationale: One-off measurements and logs retained for human review; no guest disk or linked test product is cached across runs.

entries.step: Upload installed guest disk for the restore job
entries.rationale: soldr#3295 cache-feasibility measurement: hands the installed evaluation disk to this run's restore job only, with 1-day retention, and the run's delete-disk job removes it. It deliberately never enters the Actions cache, whose budget it could not fit.

entries.step: Download Linux MSVC cross-build artifact for the restored guest
entries.rationale: Gives the restored-image job the same verified test archive and native Nextest executable as the cold guest in this one dispatch run; never restored by a later build.

entries.step: Upload restored-image measurements and guest log
entries.rationale: One-off restored-image measurements and logs retained for human review.
